profile_text.body:
Modular is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Los Altos, California. Its site describes a unified AI inference stack that runs from custom GPU kernels to production cloud serving, with the company saying it works across GPUs, CPUs, and ASICs and is engineered for demanding inference workloads. Modular says the same model and the same codebase run across NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium, TPU, Qualcomm, Intel, ARM, and Apple silicon, and it claims 2x performance.

The company's platform is MAX, which it says runs 1000+ models such as DeepSeek and Kimi out of the box, with PyTorch-like model APIs for porting custom models. Workloads can run in Modular's hosted cloud or in a customer's VPC, and the company says its forward-deployed engineers optimize each deployment. Mojo appears alongside MAX, described on the site as a language for AI development. The site lists team members including Chris, credited with founding and scaling LLVM, Clang, MLIR, Cloud TPUs, and the Swift programming language, with work at Apple, Google, SiFive, and Tesla; Tim, who worked on Google Brain and Core Systems infrastructure including TensorFlow, XLA, MLIR, TFRT, and JAX; Mostafa, formerly an engineering director at NVIDIA working on cuDNN and CUTLASS and later VP of Software at SiFive; Eric, who led TensorFlow API, compiler, and runtime teams and the productionization of JAX; and Mike, most recently at Apple and a board member of the LLVM Foundation. The site also carries a customer quote about bringing GenAI innovations to market faster for AWS customers, and a quote from a former Keras core developer now at Kyutai.

On the legal side, no litigation cases are recorded against the company. Its legal exposure listing names California, with a count of 281.
